text:
Mikhail Sergachev is Utah's workhorse, 24 minutes and 50 seconds a night and more than 26 over his last ten games, and the power play runs through him: 14 of his 25 points have come with the extra man.

The goals are the part to treat with care. He has seven on 3.8 expected goals, shooting 10.4% against 6% last season and a normal of about 7% by our numbers. That rarely lasts for a defenseman, and his scoring rate, 2.24 points per 60, sits above the range we'd expect him to hold. His last ten games have produced five points, which already looks more like the long-run Sergachev.

What's steady is the puck-moving. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 94th percentile among defensemen for setting up shots last season and better than average at stopping entries at his own line. The worry is the other side: the defensemen he plays like tend to give up chances, and Utah's five-on-five numbers are slightly better without him. A two-time Cup winner in Tampa, he's being asked to carry a lot more here. Our range has him at 61 to 84 points.
